usaaio.title: USA–North America AI Olympiad
usaaio.lead: USA-NA-AIO, run by the USA AI Olympiad (USAAIO), is an individual competition for middle and high school students in the US and Canada. It is the only pathway to Team USA at the international AI olympiads.
usaaio.disclaimer: ResAI is an independent education provider and is not affiliated with USAAIO. Facts below are summarized from usaaio.org.
usaaio.pathLead: Each round is by invitation based on the round before. Every round is taken onsite with a proctor.

r1.title: Round 1
r1.body: Open to all eligible students. A non-coding part followed by a coding part in Google Colab.

r2.title: Round 2
r2.body: By invitation. Longer, deeper problems, including open-ended modeling tasks. Awards include Camper, Gold, Silver, and Bronze.

camp.title: Round 3: Camp
camp.body: Top Round 2 students attend the USAAIO camp for training and final selection.

team.title: Team USA
team.body: Team USA represents the United States at the IOAI, IAIO, and IAI²O.

eligibility.e1: US or Canadian citizens or permanent residents, or full-time middle or high school students studying in the US or Canada.
eligibility.e2: Under 20 years old by August 30 of the competition year.
eligibility.e3: Not a full-time university student during the competition year.

usaaio.datesNote: Round 1 registration costs $50; fee waivers are available for financial hardship. Always confirm dates on usaaio.org.

format.f1: Part 1, non-coding (60 minutes): 20 multiple-choice or fill-in-the-blank problems, 150 points.
format.f2: Part 2, coding (75 minutes): tasks solved in Google Colab on CPUs.
format.f3: Topics: math for AI, Python, machine learning, PyTorch, deep learning, and CNNs.

ioai.title: International Olympiad in Artificial Intelligence
ioai.lead: IOAI brings together top high school AI students from around the world. Team USA is selected through USA-NA-AIO.
ioai.whatBody: IOAI tasks are practical machine-learning problems scored on hidden test data, solved under strict time and compute limits.

what.w1: Each task is a notebook with data, a baseline, and a scoring metric.
what.w2: Tasks cover vision, language, speech, generative models, and robustness.
what.w3: Strong solutions combine solid fundamentals with creative modeling under tight constraints.
